notes.summary: Reconstructed ordinary CLD product/support lemmas with exact degrees, localized middle-positive decomposition and coefficient-measure bounds; all original fields and singularities retained, no universal BT inference.
notes.detailedSummary: Using complete immediate units in the retained full CLDv2 source, reconstructs the weighted bound |<bT,beta>|<=integral|b|dmu_(T,eta), the smooth multiplier identity, defect support off an explicitly closed nonsmooth locus, and the exact analytic test-support principle. No supplied theorem grant, density, reduction or nonsmooth wedge is used.
notes.text:
Ordinary calculus for the new removability argument. Work over any complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, on an ordinary open N of a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space X, n>=2. Put D=d'd'', let T be an original positive doubly closed (p,p)-current, 0<=p<=n-1, and put q=n-p, r=q-1. Tests for T have degree (q,q); tests for D(hT) have degree (r,r). No reduction, normalization, scalar extension or tropical pushforward is performed, and the canonical integration current retains its actual generic Artinian lengths.

Published premises checked in their complete immediate statements/proofs in the full retained CLD source: Chambert-Loir--Ducros, arXiv:1204.6277v2, cover dated 25 July 2025 (retained internal title dated 29 July 2025, 0h06). CLD 11.1.7 and 15.7.1--2 provide ordinary analytic-domain restriction and canonical level-n calculus for separated pure analytic spaces, without a nontrivial-valuation or reducedness assumption. CLD 15.2.2--9 gives local differential separation, compact smooth cutoffs and scalar density; no global paracompactness is needed for compact localization. CLD 6.5.2 decomposes a symmetric compact diagonal smooth form into two middle-positive compact smooth forms, with its support hypothesis satisfied on good analytic domains. CLD 7.1.1--9 gives complementary-test currents, symmetry, restriction, smooth products, the ordinary sheaf property and support. CLD 7.2.8, 7.2.11--12 gives unique positive coefficient Radon measures and the ordinary Borel product. CLD 7.7.1--8 gives differential duality <DS,alpha>=<S,Dalpha>, locality and DJ=JD. Smooth J/Leibniz signs come from complete proofs of 1.3.6 and 3.3.10--11. These are published calculus inputs, not incoming note correctness grants. Recursive analytic dimension, canonical-calibration, positivity, Radon representation and Stone-Weierstrass foundations are disclosed, not claimed newly proved.

Localized decomposition: if beta is a symmetric compact (q,q)-test supported in an ordinary O subset N, apply 6.5.2 on O and extend its compact outputs by zero to N. This gives beta=eta_+-eta_- with compact middle-positive eta_+,eta_- supported in O. Extension is smooth because compact support is closed in the Hausdorff N and contained in O. No assertion of exact equality of output support with beta's support is needed.

Weighted product bound: let eta=eta_++eta_-. For continuous b, the ordinary product satisfies
|<bT,beta>| <= integral |b| d mu_(T,eta) <= sup_(supp eta)|b| <T,eta>.
Proof: the coefficient measures for eta_+ and eta_- are positive and compact. Smooth scalar density and uniqueness identify their sum with the coefficient measure for eta. The ordinary product pairs b by the difference of the two integrals. The triangle inequality gives the first bound; each measure is supported on its test support and has mass <T,eta_+> or <T,eta_->, by a smooth cutoff equal to one there. This proves the second bound using exactly the middle cone.

Smooth multiplier identity: if g is ordinary smooth on N, then D(gT)=T wedge Dg. For a symmetric compact (r,r)-test alpha put A=g d''alpha-d''g wedge alpha. The Leibniz rule gives Dg wedge alpha-g Dalpha=-d'A+C, where C=d'g wedge d''alpha+d''g wedge d'alpha. The J identities give JC=-C. Symmetry of T kills C, and d'T=0 kills d'A. Current duality and smooth multiplication prove the identity. Both first closedness equations are retained as hypotheses; no misindexed printed 8.5.3 statement is applied. Consequently Dg=0 implies D(gT)=0.

Defect support: if Z is ordinary closed and continuous h is ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian on N\Z, then R=D(hT) is symmetric, by DJ=JD, and vanishes on N\Z by the smooth multiplier identity and restriction. Thus supp R is contained in Z. If chi is smooth and equals one near Z intersect supp alpha, then <R,alpha>=<R,chi alpha>, since (1-chi)alpha is compact with support disjoint from Z. No order-zero assertion about R is required.

The other checked premise needed below is the exact CLD 15.2.1 support principle: the support of a type (a,b) G-form on a topologically separated analytic space lies in {x:d_K(x)>=max(a,b)} and does not meet a closed analytic locus Y in an analytic domain when dim Y<max(a,b). Ordinary forms are G-forms. Its proof combines the tropical chart dimension bound with 3.3.6, then d_K(y)<=dim Y. Here d_K is residual transcendence degree plus rational value-group rank; the dimension is analytic dimension, not a coarse skeleton dimension. CLD 7.3.1 and 7.7.4 also give positivity and double closedness of the original canonical integration current on a boundaryless space.

notes.summary: New direct cutoff removability bound for arbitrary positive doubly closed ordinary currents, conditional on off-locus smooth harmonicity and vanishing weighted errors; a nonzero detector with smooth trace forces inverse-oscillation cutoff-mass blowup.
notes.detailedSummary: For every actual compact test alpha and cutoff chi=1 near Z intersect supp alpha, decomposes D(chi alpha) into positive tests and proves |<D(hT),alpha>|<=integral|h-g|dmu_(T,eta). Defines a finite but not uniformly bounded cutoff mass infimum; proves smooth-trace removability and C>=d/omega for a detector of size d. No existence of vanishing certificates for arbitrary pairs is established.
notes.text:
New quantitative removability result, conditional rather than a solution of P21.3. Use the original ambient domain, field and arbitrary positive doubly closed T of n1, with q=n-p and r=q-1. Assume Z subset N is ordinary closed and h is continuous on N and ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian on N\Z. Let alpha be any symmetric compact ordinary smooth (r,r)-test, and set S=Z intersect supp alpha, a compact set.

For any ordinary neighborhood O of S, choose an actual compact ordinary smooth chi supported in O, with 0<=chi<=1 and chi=1 near S. Cutoffs exist by n1; smooth composition enforces the range bound. The form D(chi alpha) has type (q,q), is symmetric and compact in O, so n1 gives a decomposition D(chi alpha)=eta_+-eta_- into actual compact middle-positive forms supported in O. Put eta=eta_++eta_-. Let g be any ordinary smooth zero-Hessian function on the same fixed N. Then the original upstairs product obeys
|<D(hT),alpha>| <= integral_N |h-g| d mu_(T,eta) <= sup_(supp eta)|h-g| <T,eta>.

Complete proof: n1 shows R=D(hT) is supported in Z, so <R,alpha>=<R,chi alpha>. Differential duality gives <R,chi alpha>=<hT,D(chi alpha)>. The smooth multiplier identity in n1 gives <gT,D(chi alpha)>=<D(gT),chi alpha>=0. Therefore the detecting pairing equals <(h-g)T,D(chi alpha)>. The weighted ordinary-product bound of n1 proves both inequalities. All objects are actual analytic forms and the ordinary order-zero product on N, so all analytic-unit presentations represent the same tests. No nonsmooth wedge, current extension, current exhaustion or tropical equality is substituted.

It follows that D(hT)=0 if, for every alpha, a sequence or net of these actual triples on the fixed N has integral |h-g_j| d mu_(T,eta_j) tending to zero. The stronger scalar condition sup_(supp eta_j)|h-g_j| times <T,eta_j> tending to zero suffices. The proof applies the displayed bound to a fixed left side and then tests all symmetric alpha, which detect the symmetric defect. There is no requirement that g_j approximate h off the cutoff supports. Existence of the vanishing triples is an extra hypothesis; it is not inferred from D[h]=0.

A sharper obstruction bound follows. Define C_(T,alpha)(S;O) as the infimum of <T,eta_++eta_-> over exactly these cutoffs and positive decompositions, all supported in O. This number is finite and nonnegative for every O: at least one competitor exists and each compact test has a finite current value. It is zero if S is empty. It is nondecreasing when O is made smaller, since competitors are removed. Finiteness for each neighborhood does not imply a bounded family on shrinking neighborhoods.

Fix a smooth zero-Hessian g on N and let O be relatively compact in N. Put omega_g(O)=sup_O |h-g|, finite by continuity. The inequality for every competitor gives, on taking the infimum without assuming attainment,
|<D(hT),alpha>| <= omega_g(O) C_(T,alpha)(S;O).
Thus a family O_j with omega_g(O_j) C_(T,alpha)(S;O_j) tending to zero forces the detecting pairing to vanish. If h=g on S, arbitrarily small-oscillation neighborhoods exist by continuity and compactness: intersect a relatively compact neighborhood of S with {|h-g|<epsilon}. A uniformly bounded family of cutoff masses is then sufficient. Constants are allowed reference g, so locally constant traces are included. A local smooth harmonic trace extension also works after ordinary localization.

Conversely, if a detecting pairing has absolute value d>0, every relatively compact O with omega_g(O)>0 must have C_(T,alpha)(S;O)>=d/omega_g(O). An O with omega_g(O)=0 is impossible for such a detector. Therefore if h=g on S, every sequence of small-oscillation neighborhoods forces the cutoff masses to infinity in the presence of a nonzero detector. This is a necessary derivative-weighted cutoff-mass blowup, not a claim that T has an atom on Z. It does not exhibit a detector or a counterexample.

If the hypotheses and vanishing tests hold on an ordinary cover of a specified W, restriction and the current sheaf property yield D(hT)=0 on W. Only already proved identities of the original current are glued. A cover is not promoted to a basis or to an every-open result. The theorem treats all p, including scalar detecting tests when p=n-1, all fields and original nonreduced weights, but its off-locus regularity and vanishing cutoff conditions remain unproved for arbitrary original pairs and currents.

notes.summary: Proves degree-specific analytic-locus removability when dim Z<n-p-1 and h is ordinary smooth zero-Hessian off Z; identifies the residual dimensional window and explicitly leaves the entire original P21.3 unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual analytic partial theorem for arbitrary allowed currents and both valuations, including nonreduced spaces, obtained by defect support and exact CLD test-support vanishing. It excludes no nonempty locus at p=n-1. For p>=1, n-p-1<=dim Z<n-1 remains unexcluded by this method despite canonical nullity. No arbitrary-pair regularity or cutoff bound, universal proof, or admissible analytic counterexample is produced; candidate is false.
notes.text:
Analytic dimension consequence and exact negative completion decision. Let W be any specified ordinary open in the unchanged original ambient X, let 0<=p<=n-1, and set r=n-p-1. Suppose Z subset W is ordinary closed and locally a closed analytic locus of dimension strictly less than r, and h is continuous on W and ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian on W\Z. Then D(hT)=0 for every original positive doubly closed ordinary (p,p)-current T on W. In particular the required BT equality holds for any separately admissible finite continuous psh pair U,V with difference h satisfying these extra conditions.

Complete proof: n1 gives supp D(hT) subset Z. On every ordinary neighborhood carrying the stated analytic-locus bound, CLD 15.2.1(b), as stated and checked in n1, says the support of each compact smooth (r,r) detecting test is disjoint from Z. That test therefore pairs to zero with the defect by the current support definition. All complementary tests vanish, so the defect is zero on the neighborhood; ordinary sheaf localization proves zero on W. The same proof applies to an arbitrary closed ordinary Z under the explicit pointwise condition d_K(z)<r, using 15.2.1(a). It does not assign an analytic dimension to an arbitrary skeleton or closed set. No assertion that canonical Hessian nullity alone implies the off-locus smooth-Hessian condition is made.

For a locus of pure analytic codimension c the sufficient integer bound is c>=p+2. For n=2, p=0 allows zero-dimensional analytic loci, whereas p=1 allows no nonempty locus. For n=3 the respective upper dimension bounds are one, zero and no nonempty locus. In all dimensions p=n-1 gives r=0 and hence no nonempty-locus conclusion. This is an arbitrary-current partial result, not a resolution of the universal atom.

There is also a necessary location statement, now assuming off-locus smooth zero-Hessian regularity without imposing the preceding dimension inequality. If the defect is nonzero, the definition of a nonzero current provides a compact smooth detecting test; symmetry permits its symmetric part. Its support must meet Z or it would pair to zero. The CLD support principle says each point in that support has d_K>=r. Thus an actual nonzero detector must meet Z at a point of d_K at least n-p-1. For a closed analytic locus the local dimension cannot everywhere be below that threshold.

Applying the proved removability result to the original canonical integration current delta_X, which is positive and doubly closed by n1, shows D[h]=0 whenever the analytic locus has dimension <n-1. This uses the original calibration with actual generic Artinian lengths, not unit-weight reduction. It does not show h or -h is psh, or supply admissible U,V. For p>=1, the interval n-p-1 <= dim Z < n-1 is therefore a possible dimensional window in this off-locus route where canonical nullity is established but dimensional support alone does not prove multiplier independence. This identifies unexcluded possibilities, not a counterexample. No such window occurs for p=0.

The direct weighted-cutoff argument of n2 succeeds as an exact bound but does not close the universal gap: neither off-locus ordinary smooth zero-Hessian regularity nor vanishing weighted cutoff errors or uniform small-neighborhood cutoff mass is proved for arbitrary continuous equal-curvature differences and arbitrary currents. In particular pointwise finiteness of every cutoff mass cannot be exchanged for a uniform bound. The critical dimension permits detecting tests; that permission does not manufacture a defect. No compatible positive closed exhaustion, harmonic-test lift with ordinary-product agreement, generated-psh recognition of both signs, or ascent and faithful descent of the original current has been constructed.

The full original P21.3 remains unresolved. Its every-open/every-current assertion retains all complete fields including trivial valuation, strict/good/separated/boundaryless and pure n>=2 hypotheses, singularities and nilpotents, actual generic lengths, all p=0,...,n-1, and separately admissible finite continuous psh U,V with exact upstairs D[U]=D[V]. No actual analytic X,U,V,T and compact smooth alpha with a nonzero detecting pairing has been exhibited. The dossier's previously removed curves, polycylinders, invariant split-toric ranges and stated approximation classes are not claimed as new solutions. No cover is turned into a basis. Accordingly candidate=false.
